items.title: Australia could still buy five US submarines if needed, defence minister says
items.description: Defence Minister Richard Marles has defended a shake-up to AUKUS that would involve Australia buying three second-hand Virginia-class submarines from the United States.

items.title: France detains 780 after deadly riots follow PSG's Champions League win

featured_image.name: Paris police detain dozens after violence erupts during celebrations of PSG's  Champions League title

items.description: Paris Saint-Germain's second consecutive Champions League title — sealed in a dramatic penalty shootout against Arsenal in Budapest on Saturday — triggered one of the most violent nights of football-related disorder France has seen, with 780 people arrested and one person found dead on the Paris ring road.

items.title: Iran's Pezeshkian reportedly resigns, citing IRGC takeover

featured_image.name: Pezeshkian: Iran with a different face?

items.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has reportedly submitted a formal letter of resignation to the office of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, claiming he has been systematically excluded from key decision-making and that hardline factions within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps have seized control of government affairs, according to Iran International, which cited an anonymous Iranian official. Iranian authorities quickly denied the report.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Live: Pauline Hanson says she has 'the ability' to be PM
items.description: Pauline Hansonsays she has the ability to lead the nation as prime minister but admits she was shocked by a poll that suggested One Nation had pulled ahead of Labor. Follow live.

items.title: Supreme leader hard to find as Trump wants peace plan rewrites
items.description: Donald Trump is reported to be amending a peace plan, which could fuel further delays in finding a final agreement.

items.title: Three-year-old child dies in Melbourne house fire
items.description: A child has died in a house fire in Werribee and another person has been taken to hospital with serious injuries.

items.title: Conviction of Aussie band's 'sixth member' reveals Byron Bay's dark side as women speak out
items.description: Rachel Kila has waived her right to anonymity to join dozens of others speaking out about the experiences of young girls in Byron Bay in the early 2000s, where they say it became normalised for older boys and men to groom and have sex with girls then publicly humiliate them.

items.title: Why is Labor spending its political majority on this tax reform?
items.description: Why has Labor decided to spend the political capital of a large majority on a minor change to capital gains tax on businesses?

items.title: Quietly published Liberal Party paper raises gender membership concerns
items.description: The Liberal Party has quietly published a paper that floats offering a cut price $10 digital membership to join the party, in an effort to offset its declining numbers.

items.title: Sydney and Melbourne property values drop as housing market stalls in May
items.description: Australia's housing market continues to lose momentum, with national home values flatlining in May as higher interest rates, weak confidence and proposed property tax changes weigh on demand.

items.title: 'Caught lying': Police bashed a man, then charged him with assaulting them
items.description: After fracturing about a dozen of a man's ribs and puncturing his lung, police officers discussed how to explain what happened to him.

items.title: Taiwan vows not to be 'silenced' after China expels NYT reporter

featured_image.name: China Expelled Reporter Over NYT Interview With Taiwan President

items.description: Taiwan's Presidential Office on Sunday condemned China's expulsion of New York Times correspondent Vivian Wang, declaring the island democracy "will not be silenced because of oppression" and vowing to continue engaging with international media despite Beijing's pressure campaign against foreign journalists.[1][2]

items.title: Hegseth warns U.S. ready to resume strikes on Iran if talks fail

featured_image.name: Watch: US defence chief Pete Hegseth speaks at Shangri-La Dialogue in  Singapore - CNA

items.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned Saturday that the United States is fully prepared to restart military operations against Iran if ongoing ceasefire negotiations collapse, delivering a pointed message at the Shangri-La Dialogue security forum in Singapore as tensions in the region escalated with a fresh Iranian missile strike on a base housing American personnel.

items.title: Israel seizes Beaufort Castle in deepest Lebanon incursion in 25 years

featured_image.name: Israeli troops have captured the strategic Crusader-built Beaufort Castle  in southern Lebanon, the military announces, as the IDF further expands its  ground offensive against Hezbollah. The IDF says that it launched a

items.description: Israeli forces have captured the medieval Beaufort Castle and pushed past the Litani River into southern Lebanon, marking the country's deepest ground incursion into its northern neighbor in more than 25 years. The advance, confirmed by the Israeli military on Sunday, has shattered a fragile ceasefire and drawn sweeping evacuation orders covering much of southern Lebanon.

items.title: Trump returned Iran peace draft with stricter conditions

featured_image.name: Trump holds situation room meeting on Iran nuclear deal negotiations

items.description: President Donald Trump returned a revised draft of a proposed peace agreement to Tehran with stricter conditions after a two-hour meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on Friday, extending negotiations into at least another week, according to multiple reports.

items.title: Blast at explosives storage site kills dozens in Myanmar

featured_image.name: Blast kills dozens in village in rebel-held region of Myanmar

items.description: An explosion at a building storing mining explosives in northeastern Myanmar killed at least 46 people on Sunday, including six children, with local media reporting death tolls as high as 55. About 70 others were injured in the blast, which struck around noon in the village of Kaungtup in Namhkam township, roughly two miles from the Chinese border.

items.title: One Nation overtakes Labor for first time as young Australians reject budget
items.description: Labor's federal budget is falling flat with its target demographic as millennials say they would rather vote for One Nation than Labor or the Greens, according to a new Redbridge poll.

items.title: Lula rejects U.S. terrorist label for Brazil's largest gangs

featured_image.name: Lula blasts US for labelling Brazil crime factions as terrorists

items.description:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Friday denounced the United States' decision to designate two of Brazil's largest criminal organizations as terrorist groups, calling it undue interference in the country's internal affairs and warning Washington against treating Brazil "like a banana republic."

"We will not accept being treated like children, we will not accept being treated as if we were a banana republic," Lula said at a public event on Friday, referring to "a certain Marco Rubio, who said that our criminals are terrorists and that Americans can intervene".[1][2]

items.title: Philippines says China threat persists despite Trump-Xi summit

featured_image.name: Philippines defence chief Gilberto Teodoro Jr calls out China's 'propaganda  spiel' at Shangri-La Dialogue | The Straits Times

items.description: The Philippines' defense secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said on Saturday that the country remains under "severe threat" from China, declaring that a recent thaw in U.S.-China relations following the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing has done nothing to ease tensions in the South China Sea.[1][2]

items.title: Quarter of trapped oil tankers slip out of Hormuz

featured_image.name: A Quarter of Large Oil Tankers Trapped by Iran War Have ...

items.description: A slow, stealthy trickle of oil tankers has begun slipping out of the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, with roughly one-quarter of the large non-Iranian vessels stranded since the war began now having crossed the chokepoint, even as Chevron CEO Mike Wirth warned that ships continue to come under attack.

items.description: President Trump states the U.S. military conducted its first known airstrike inside Venezuela targeting a dock where drugs were allegedly loaded onto boats[1][2][4].

items.description: President Trump met with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to discuss advancing phase two of the Gaza ceasefire, including reconstruction and responses to Iran[1][4].

items.description: China prioritizes humanoid robots in tech race with U.S., ramping up production while warning of industry bubble and potential bottlenecks[3].
